title: DNS names form a tree, with data in resource records
summary: DNS names form a tree, with data in resource records.
body: RFC 1034 describes the domain name space and resource records as a tree-structured name space and the data associated with the names. Conceptually, each node and leaf of the tree has a label. The source says: "Elements of the DNS The DNS has three major components: - The DOMAIN NAME SPACE and RESOURCE RECORDS, which are specifications for a tree structured name space and data associated with the names." The hierarchy is the specification's structure. A name is a path in that tree, not a free-form string with no parent.

sources.title: RFC 1034: Domain Names — Concepts and Facilities
